title: Pakistan's Double Game: Iranian Jets Sheltered at Nur Khan
excerpt: US officials allege Islamabad quietly harbored Iranian military aircraft as it posed as a neutral peace broker between Washington and Tehran.
body:
Pakistan secretly allowed Iranian military aircraft to park at one of its most strategic air bases even as Islamabad publicly presented itself as a neutral mediator between Washington and Tehran — a revelation that has rattled US officials and put the ceasefire under fresh strain.

**What happened:**
US officials told CBS News that days after President Trump announced a ceasefire with Iran in early April, Tehran sent multiple aircraft to Pakistan's Nur Khan Air Base, including an Iranian Air Force RC-130 — a reconnaissance and intelligence-gathering variant of the C-130 Hercules. The movements reflected an apparent effort to insulate some of Iran's remaining military and aviation assets from the expanding conflict, even as officials publicly served as brokers for de-escalation.

**Pakistan pushes back — but scrutiny grows:**
A senior Pakistani official rejected the claims, telling CBS News that 'Nur Khan base is right in the heart of the city' and that a large fleet of aircraft parked there could not be hidden from public view. Senator Lindsey Graham swiftly questioned Islamabad's role, calling for a complete reevaluation of Pakistan's actions as a mediator between Iran, the United States, and other parties. Islamabad has attempted to navigate both sides of the crisis — presenting itself to Washington as a stabilizing intermediary while avoiding steps that could alienate Tehran or China, Iran's most powerful international backer.

**Why the stakes are high:**
The revelations underscore the increasingly fragile geopolitical balancing act facing Pakistan as Islamabad attempts to maintain ties with the United States, Iran, Gulf Arab states, and China while avoiding a widening regional conflict. The rejection of Iran's peace proposal has further strained what seems to be a ceasefire in name only, as Trump prepares to travel to Beijing for talks where the war in Iran is expected to feature prominently alongside disputes over trade and Taiwan.

**What to watch:**
Watch whether US Central Command responds formally to the CBS allegations, and whether Trump's Beijing summit produces a unified push — or a fracture — in the fragile ceasefire framework.
